description:
We’re building a curious, collaborative team for the NASA Space Apps Challenge.

 Looking for teammates interested in coding, AI, design, research, or space. The

 goal is to learn together, turn an idea into a working prototype, and have fun

 building. You don’t need to know everything—just be willing to contribute!
summary: Left Behind is an interactive, source-led web documentary about NASA equipment that remains on the Moon and Mars. A guided journey connects each machine’s purpose, why it stayed, its documented status and scientific legacy. Visitors explore sourced locations, inspect NASA reference models and mission imagery, and open evidence behind individual claims. A separate deep-space collection keeps orbital and interplanetary missions distinct from surface equipment. The goal is engaging space-history learning with visible evidence, uncertainty and asset provenance.
details:
PROJECT DETAILS

Try it: https://left-behind-tau.vercel.app

Source code: https://github.com/aditya-zig/left-behind

What we developed. Left Behind presents NASA equipment left on the Moon and Mars as an interactive educational documentary for space enthusiasts, including school-age learners. Instead of treating retired hardware as forgotten objects, it connects engineering decisions to the discoveries the equipment made possible.

The experience. Visitors choose a world, follow a guided journey or explore manually, select sourced locations, and open equipment stories. Mission dialogs bring together purpose, why hardware stayed, documented status, scientific legacy, NASA reference models or official imagery, and sources supporting specific claims. The public project documents 13 Moon/Mars equipment stories, 29 map locations (19 Moon and 10 Mars), and an 18-record archive. Five beyond-Moon/Mars records are kept separate rather than plotted as lunar or Martian surface equipment.

How it works. React and TypeScript organize typed mission records, source links and interface state. Three.js renders NASA-textured planetary views; Google model-viewer supports reference-model inspection. Vite builds a static application hosted on Vercel. Assets, fonts and the Draco decoder are bundled locally. No account, API key or database is required. Text, mission lists and evidence links are primary content; browser/device speech is optional. Motion controls and manual exploration let visitors set their pace.

NASA evidence in use. Challenge-listed NSSDCA records supply Apollo design facts, landing references, rover traverse/sample totals and ALSEP history. NASA Science supplies robotic mission histories and discoveries. NASA-distributed models, imagery and the SVS CGI Moon Kit provide visual context. Per-file manifests record source/download URLs, retrieval information and SHA-256 checksums. The in-app source register and source-to-claim descriptions make provenance inspectable.

Original work and creativity. The project’s contribution is its source-led documentary structure, guided journeys, interactive collection and evidence-first presentation. NASA resources are integrated into stories, geography and inspection, rather than included only as a bibliography.

Benefits and intended impact. We aim to make NASA’s equipment legacy understandable and engaging, and help visitors ask what a machine did, why it remains, and what scientists learned. These are intended benefits, not measured learning outcomes. Future work includes educator feedback, accessibility/user evaluation and additional source-reviewed stories.

Honest limits. This is not live spacecraft monitoring, navigation software, a deployed cleanup mission or a georeferenced reconstruction. Routes are illustrative; coordinate precision varies. Reference models may show earlier or complete configurations: for example, NASA’s full lunar-module model includes the ascent stage that departed, while only the descent stage remained. Photographs and NASA-published artist concepts are distinguished. No equipment prices, current-health telemetry, life-detection claims, user-study results or impact metrics are invented. NASA does not sponsor or endorse this independent project.

AI ASSISTANCE DISCLOSURE

AI tools assisted software implementation, research organization and educational wording. The project’s mission claims are linked to NASA and other source records for inspection rather than being treated as authoritative AI output. No AI-generated space imagery, videos or equipment models were created for the project. NASA-published imagery and NASA-distributed reference models retain their source/contributor credits. Optional browser/device speech synthesis is not a recorded human or astronaut performance. The fictional Orbit guide is interface content, not a NASA character or quotation.

This seven-slide presentation’s wording, layout and generation script were also AI-assisted. Its product images are actual captures of the public deployment, not AI-generated space imagery. AI assistance is acknowledged in the PowerPoint metadata and speaker notes as well as this description. Project source/asset provenance is documented in the public credits and manifests.

NASA RESOURCES AND THEIR USE

The official challenge Resources tab explicitly lists the NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA). Left Behind uses its records as working evidence:

- Apollo 11 / 1969-059C: two-stage lunar-module design, descent stage left behind, landing coordinates, sample mass and chronology.

- Apollo 15 / 1971-063C and the LRV reference: rover deployment, engineering, traverse distance, sample total and landing-site reference. Landing coordinates are not misrepresented as the rover’s final parking position.

- Apollo 12 ALSEP / 1969-099C and the lunar landing-site catalogue: deployment, experiment suite, power, shutdown and a location distinguished from the lunar module.

NASA Science mission pages support robotic mission histories, findings and distinct last-contact/mission-closure dates. NASA 3D Resources supplies ten reference GLBs and associated imagery/previews; originals are pinned to commit 11ebb4ee043715aefbba6aeec8a61746fad67fa7. NASA/GSFC/SVS CGI Moon Kit (SVS 4720, LRO camera/laser-altimeter teams, Ernie Wright) supplies the equirectangular lunar texture. NASA Image and Video Library and mission pages supply photographs and published imagery. NASA Trek is an outbound reference for authoritative geographic exploration, not an embedded data layer or a mapping service created by this project.

Source-to-claim methodology, in-app records and per-file manifests expose how these resources are used. Coordinates are contextual, not navigation-grade; imagery and model limitations remain visible.
